completion_scope.selected_lake_or_reservoir_passage: No selected lake, reservoir or salar passage is indicated by the inspected cartography.
completion_scope.precision_scope: Ordinary generalized drainage corridor and component scale. The modeled opening extends slightly beyond a cartographic head-arm tip, and parts of lower Carrizalillo are offset within the mapped branching valley; these do not establish exact endpoint, bank or branch-by-branch equivalence. completion_scope.flow_scope: Mapped quebrada continuity is a drainage-corridor observation, not a claim of perennial flow. The historical CONAF prose explicitly characterizes runoff as occasional.

records.region: Atacama, Chile; Agua de la Piedra–Juncal–Carrizalillo–Pan de Azúcar dry-drainage corridor to the Pacific.
records.candidate_name_role: Representative identity anchored in the downstream coastal quebrada of the connected selected dry-drainage system; not a uniform hydronym for the initial head arm, Agua de la Piedra, Juncal or Carrizalillo components.
records.geographic_disambiguation: The selected northeastern head arm enters Agua de la Piedra, continues west through Juncal and the Carrizo junction into Carrizalillo, then through the Doña Inés Chica joining setting to the lower Pan de Azúcar quebrada and Pacific coast. Original official hydrographic maps cover the entire generalized drainage corridor and its material junctions; the CONAF original park map supplies independent coastal-setting correspondence. Quebrada Pan de Azúcar is supported only as the representative downstream/system identity.
records.supported_name_scope: Representative identity anchored in the downstream coastal quebrada of the connected selected dry-drainage system; not a uniform hydronym for the initial head arm, Agua de la Piedra, Juncal or Carrizalillo components.

component_scope_limits: The short initial head arm has no independently established hydronym; retain its name as null.
Agua de la Piedra, Juncal and Carrizalillo are upstream component names and are not replaced by the representative downstream name.
The geographic corridor is established at ordinary map scale; the model’s local offsets are not represented as precise channel alignment or a surveyed connection between individual banks.
The lower official map labels Pan de Azúcar, while the CONAF park map writes Quebrada Pan de Azúcar. Neither source makes every upstream segment uniformly Pan de Azúcar.
Unselected tributaries, including Carrizo and Doña Inés Chica, remain contextual junctions rather than renamed selected tributary features.
No present-day discharge, flood condition, wetness, legal name registration, official river length or exact active mouth is inferred.

records.completion_scope: All selected FID 13812 components, including the opening, principal tributary junctions, lower diversion choice and actual terminal, are covered at ordinary generalized corridor scale. No genuine selected component or connector gap remains. Optional ANA source failures do not alter this completed representative finding.
records.region: Lambayeque/Cajamarca, Peru; selected Chancay–Reque river corridor.
records.candidate_name_role: Representative river-system identity for the fully mapped selected Llantén–Chancay–Reque corridor; not a uniform local name for every reach.
records.geographic_disambiguation: Independent original MTC maps establish the selected headward seasonal feeder into Río Llantén, its Catilluc–Tongod passage, the San Juan junction near Ninabamba, Río Chancay through Chancaybaños, Catache, Cumbil and Chongoyape, and the selected Río Reque branch to the Pacific by Eten. PEOT original regional cartography confirms that Tinajones is off the selected route and independently distinguishes the lower branches. The representative Río Chancay-Lambayeque identity is supported while all accepted/scalar/Korean naming and application fields remain unset.
records.supported_name_scope: Representative river-system identity for the fully mapped selected Llantén–Chancay–Reque corridor; not a uniform local name for every reach.

component_scope_limits: The opening dashed feeder is mapped but has no independently read local hydronym; its name remains null.
The San Miguel/Santa Cruz source maps use Llantén upstream and Chancay in the receiving northern valley. These source labels do not establish a surveyed or formal legal transition point.
The selected lower course is Reque. Lambayeque and Taymi are separate lower branches at La Puntilla and are not extended over the selected southern route.
Tinajones, Boró and Collique are separate reservoir settings, not named lake passages in this selected object. No name is transferred from those adjacent features.
Río Chancay-Lambayeque is a representative system identity supported by the mapped receiving trunk and independent PEOT usage, not a uniform whole-feature scalar name.
Formal registry status is unverified. No Korean translation or product-name change is proposed.

records.completion_scope: The whole selected FID10818 has primary-map correspondence at ordinary component/corridor scale. The opening is a mapped but unnamed southwestern feeder joining the Tuy near El Consejo. Independent original field cartography carries the main river continuously to the Caribbean at Boca de Paparo. No material connector or unviewed route interval remains. Optional source failures are detailed separately and create no additional pending status.
records.region: North-central Venezuela; unnamed Las Guacamayas–La Mora feeder into Río Tuy near El Consejo, then the Tuy to Boca de Paparo on the Caribbean.
records.candidate_name_role: representative receiving/main-river system identity, not a uniform whole-route scalar name
records.geographic_disambiguation: Río Tuy is supported as the representative receiving-system identity. The selected route begins with an unnamed Las Guacamayas–La Mora feeder that joins the Tuy near El Consejo, then continues through Tácata, Cúa, Ocumare and Santa Teresa to Boca de Paparo on the Caribbean. Major tributaries and the adjacent Ocumarito, Lagartijo, Quebrada Seca and Taguaza reservoirs retain separate scope. All selected components are covered at generalized corridor scale; no uniform scalar or Korean name is assigned.
records.supported_name_scope: representative receiving/main-river system identity, not a uniform whole-route scalar name

component_scope_limits: Río Tuy is only the representative receiving-system candidate.
The selected opening is not the northern Tuy headwater near Colonia Tovar; the Las Guacamayas–La Mora feeder name remains null.
Major tributaries and nearby reservoirs are not renamed after the representative river.
No legal/formal registry determination, exact reach-name boundary, modern shoreline or bank/vertex agreement is claimed.
196.269km is unchanged retained rendered-model metadata, not an official river length.

records.region: Western Venezuela; Guasare–Limón middle/lower corridor to Bahía de Urubá, with the southwestern Perijá opening unresolved.
records.candidate_name_role: Scoped candidate for the Guasare-to-Limón system represented by the selected middle and lower route; whole selected correspondence remains pending at the southwestern opening and upper connector.
records.material_pending_reason: No acquired primary map resolves the entire southwestern selected opening and upper connector to the detailed Guasare middle-valley coverage. The relevant DCN Alto Guasare/Hoja5647 catalogue request failed with Cache miss and no sheet pixels were obtained. Cerro Pintado prose and broad relief/basin context are not substituted for the missing channel connection.
records.geographic_disambiguation: Original research maps and supporting prose establish the Guasare middle valley, its distinction from the Socuy-Cachirí reservoir branch, the eastward Limón lowland/wetland corridor and the terminal into Bahía de Urubá in the El Tablazo–Maracaibo system. Río Guasare–Limón is explicitly used as a system designation in Rincón2017. The selected southwestern opening below the Cerro Pintado sector and its upper-valley connector are not sufficiently resolved by the acquired maps, so this is material pending rather than a completed naming-scope hold.
records.completion_scope: Original research maps and supporting prose establish the Guasare middle valley, its distinction from the Socuy-Cachirí reservoir branch, the eastward Limón lowland/wetland corridor and the terminal into Bahía de Urubá in the El Tablazo–Maracaibo system. Río Guasare–Limón is explicitly used as a system designation in Rincón2017. The selected southwestern opening below the Cerro Pintado sector and its upper-valley connector are not sufficiently resolved by the acquired maps, so this is material pending rather than a completed naming-scope hold.

component_scope_limits: Rincón2017 distinguishes Guasare upstream and Limón after receiving Socuy. The compounded candidate is a representative system designation, not a uniform scalar hydronym for all selected components.
Socuy and Cachirí are distinct lateral branches. Manuelote and Tulé reservoirs belong to that branch setting and are not renamed after the selected Guasare route.
The lower course is an estuarine wetland/lagoon system associated with Sinamaica and Bahía de Urubá; Sinamaica, Caño Paijana, Caño Flora, Urubá and El Tablazo are not whole-feature aliases.
The karst study reports seasonal underground flow in a middle Guasare interval. This is hydrological context; no exact subsurface alignment or modern flowing condition is asserted.
No accepted name, Korean name, official registry status, precise hydronym-transition vertex, exact shoreline/mouth vertex or official total length is established.

reconstruction_rule: Start from the pinned r46 cumulative index and apply later append-only deltas in verified commit order, rejecting duplicate IDs. publication_boundary: Own factual name/scope findings, public official URLs, bounded geometry metadata and public continuity pins only. No original maps, crops, complete coordinates or private source/derivative/registration fingerprints. Official hosting does not establish source redistribution rights.

research_order.progress_rule: Follow the actual continental order: Americas, Asia, Africa, Europe, then other, with all rivers before lakes. Preserve original queue IDs and ranks for continuity; apply documented geographic deferrals without counting them as name research, and place deferred objects into their corrected later phase by length-descending, stable-ID order. Prior candidate and scope-held assessments remain unresolved where stated.
